s9.title: 7769 The CREW | Behind the Bumpers | FRC REBUILT Robot

bet.text: A reply that reads as the team's says it builds the simplest robot that meets the objectives needed to be competitive, and calls simplicity the standout feature.

demand.text: Fuel throughput: the team credits hopper capacity of almost 70 (mostly 50 to 60 in play) and moving fuel in and out quickly for its most successful season.
At the state championship it climbed only when the climb ranking point was within reach, to avoid the risk otherwise.

cycle.text: A rack intake slides out with the hopper and pulls fuel in; belts push fuel to the injector; compliant wheels feed an S-shaped path to flywheels under a hood that pops up. Limelight pose aims the shot.
A reply that reads as the team's says jostling the intake in and out helped keep fuel from jamming in the hopper.

endgame.text: A side "harpoon" climb with auto climb, helped by a second Limelight when the front one cannot see tags. At the state championship it was off the robot because the net could stretch over and catch on it, and no climb ranking point was in reach.

fallback.text: Under defense it shoots from the trench: a reply that reads as the team's says the raised hood reacts against the trench, so the robot is not pushed underneath.
Another post says a drum only two fuel wide (the team says 2.75) was harder for defenders to exploit than very wide ones.

gave_up.text: A front "flippy hook" climb, which got in the way of the shooter rollers.
A video ranking says the 2.75-ball-wide shooter had slightly lower throughput than full-width ones on Einstein, though still a very high rate.
A reply that reads as the team's calls shearing teeth on the polycarbonate intake racks its biggest pain point, never fully fixed.

changed.text: Two separate shooters jammed, so the middle came out to make one full shooter.

Replies that read as the team's say powered top and bottom indexing rollers then jammed the chamber until the lower ones were fixed in place, and that a lower deploy current limit reduced rack breakage for the world championship.
A post from the alliance says a collision broke the shooting motors in Einstein match 13.

outcome.text: 70-5-0 in official play; won the Galileo division; captain of the Galileo alliance on Einstein; ranked 5 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 333.84, Galileo).

solves.text: Get balls inside the robot as fast as possible

facts.text: A 1/2 in hex shaft across the robot ties the two sides together
4 in polycarbonate tube wrapped in cat tongue, on two Kraken X60s

A reply that reads as the team's says the deploy current limit drops from 45 A while deploying to 5 A once deployed, to make the intake more collapsible

cost.text: A reply that reads as the team's says rack teeth, trouble free at two events, sheared every two to three matches at the state championship; about 16 spare arms were made for the world championship, where they still sheared but less often; the writer would try decoupling the two sides next
